metadata.purpose: Per-target modality annotation for Parkinson's disease. Tells the design layer which proteins a small molecule can realistically engage.

schema.small_molecule_tractability: 0-1 ordinal prior that a drug-like small molecule can productively engage this protein; 0 marks a transcriptional readout rather than a target
schema.note: the reason for the value, so it can be argued with

metadata.curation_rule: Ordinal priors reflecting precedent in the public literature, on the same scale as the MS annotation. Judgements, not measurements.
metadata.readout_convention: A target scoring below 0.2 is treated by the design engine as a readout: the profile may require its expression to move, but no arm of a designed molecule will be assigned to bind it.
metadata.the_defining_problem: Alpha-synuclein, the central protein in the disease, is intrinsically disordered and scores 0.25. Parkinson's is therefore a sharper test of the tractability floor than multiple sclerosis: the most important target is one a small molecule largely cannot reach, and the profile has to route around it through lysosomal and autophagic mechanisms instead.

ACSL4.note: Drives ferroptotic lipid peroxidation; inhibitors reported

AIF1.note: Iba1; the standard microglial activation marker

ALDH1A1.note: Detoxifies reactive dopamine metabolites; inhibitor chemotypes exist, activation wanted

ATP13A2.note: Lysosomal polyamine transporter; no established chemotype

BCL2.note: BH3-mimetic chemotype is mature but pro-apoptotic, the wrong direction here

BDNF.note: Induction is indirect; direct agonism unresolved

CACNA1D.note: Cav1.3; isradipine reached phase 3 and failed on efficacy, not tractability

CALB1.note: Calbindin; marks the neurons that survive, a readout not a target

CASP3.note: Executioner caspase; inhibition this late rarely rescues

CCL2.note: Its receptor is the tractable node

CDK5.note: Aberrant p25/CDK5 activation is implicated; selective inhibition over the CDK family is hard

COMT.note: Three approved inhibitors; tolcapone's hepatotoxicity is chemotype-specific

CTSD.note: Cathepsin D degrades alpha-synuclein; activation rather than inhibition is wanted

CYBB.note: NOX2; microglial superoxide source with published inhibitors

DDC.note: AADC; carbidopa and benserazide exploit peripheral selectivity

DNM1L.note: Drp1 GTPase; fission inhibitors such as the mdivi-1 chemotype exist though mechanism is disputed

DRD1.note: D1 agonists are established, with dyskinesia as the class liability

DRD2.note: The most heavily drugged target in the disease

FBXO7.note: F-box protein in the mitophagy pathway; no chemotype

FTH1.note: Ferritin heavy chain; chelators act on the iron, not the protein

GBA1.note: Glucocerebrosidase; ambroxol chaperoning and substrate-reduction chemotypes both in clinic

GDNF.note: Protein delivered surgically; not a small-molecule target

GFAP.note: Astrocyte activation marker and a fluid biomarker

GPX4.note: Ferroptosis gatekeeper; covalent chemotypes exist, activation is the wanted direction

GSK3B.note: ATP-competitive inhibitors are mature; selectivity and a narrow therapeutic index are the obstacles

HLA-DRA.note: MHC class II; antigen presentation readout

HMOX1.note: Induced downstream of Nrf2 rather than engaged directly

HSPA8.note: Hsc70; allosteric modulators reported, selectivity across the family is poor

HSPB1.note: Small heat-shock protein; no tractable pocket

IL1B.note: Reached upstream through NLRP3 and caspase-1

LAMP1.note: Lysosomal membrane marker; a readout of lysosomal mass

LAMP2.note: Chaperone-mediated autophagy receptor; largely a readout

LRRK2.note: Selective inhibitors have reached phase 2 with CNS exposure; the best-precedented disease-modifying target in the disease

MAOB.note: Three approved inhibitors; a mature chemotype

MAP1LC3B.note: LC3-II is the canonical autophagy readout, not a target

MAPT.note: Tau; aggregation inhibitors are an active but unproven class

MTOR.note: Rapalogues and ATP-competitive chemotypes both established; drives autophagic clearance

NDUFS1.note: Complex I subunit; a readout of bioenergetic state

NEFL.note: Neurofilament light; the field's neurodegeneration biomarker

NFE2L2.note: Reached covalently through KEAP1, the fumarate mechanism

NLRP3.note: Inflammasome sensor; CNS-penetrant chemotypes in clinic

OPA1.note: Fusion GTPase; activation is the useful direction

PARK7.note: DJ-1; small redox-sensor protein, weakly ligandable

PINK1.note: Kinetin-analogue activators reported; activating a kinase is far harder than inhibiting one

PPARGC1A.note: PGC-1alpha; engaged indirectly through AMPK and sirtuins

PRKN.note: Parkin; allosteric activators are reported but early

PSMD4.note: Proteasome subunit; inhibition is the wrong direction here

RAB10.note: LRRK2 phosphorylation substrate; the pharmacodynamic readout for LRRK2 inhibition

RET.note: GDNF co-receptor; agonism is the therapeutically useful direction and the difficult one

SCARB2.note: LIMP-2, the trafficking receptor for glucocerebrosidase; interface target

SLC18A2.note: VMAT2; approved inhibitors exist, though for the opposite indication

SLC6A3.note: Dopamine transporter; well-precedented but abuse liability follows the mechanism

SNCA.note: Alpha-synuclein is intrinsically disordered with no stable binding pocket. It is the central protein in the disease and among the least tractable for a small molecule, which is why the clinical programmes are antibodies and antisense. Lowering it indirectly, through lysosomal or autophagic enhancement, is the realistic small-molecule route.

SNCAIP.note: Synphilin-1; interaction partner without a pocket

SQSTM1.note: p62; an autophagic flux readout more than a pocket

STUB1.note: CHIP E3 ligase; ligase activation is an immature modality

TFEB.note: Master lysosomal regulator, reached indirectly through mTOR rather than directly

TFRC.note: Transferrin receptor; largely an antibody and delivery target

TH.note: Tyrosine hydroxylase; the rate-limiting enzyme, but its loss is the readout of neuron death

TNF.note: Small-molecule trimer disruptors exist; none approved

VPS35.note: Retromer subunit; pharmacological chaperones are early
